detail.title: Adaptive Federated Intelligence for Resource-Constrained Edge Ecosystems
detail.abstract: Edge computing setups are becoming more complex with different kinds of devices, IoT nodes, and micro-datacenters that need smart, fast local data processing. Managing AI workloads across such distributed nodes is a big challenge because the nodes have limited resources, data privacy needs to be kept, and the nodes are heterogeneous systems.This paper proposes a federated AI orchestration framework for finding, managing, and executing machine learning operations in heterogeneous edge environments. The framework uses decentralized model training, dynamic resource allocation, and cross-device workload scheduling to accomplish better performance and data privacy guarantee. Experiments on the simulated edge devices have shown that the latency of model training was reduced by 38% and the overall task throughput was increased by 32% in comparison to centralized orchestration approaches. The findings suggest that federated AI orchestration is a viable approach to improve computational efficiency, scalability, and privacy in complex edge ecosystems..

title: Platform Financing vs. Bank Financing: The Impact of Credit Rating
affiliations: and Shanghai Maritime University (SMU)

detail.title: Platform Financing vs. Bank Financing: The Impact of Credit Rating
detail.abstract: When selling through online platforms under revenue-sharing contracts, capital-constrained sellers often face the challenge of which financing scheme should be selected: traditional financing (i.e., bank financing) or the emerging platform financing? Meanwhile, credit ratings, which reflect exogenous credit risk, play a critical role in shaping financing terms. This paper examines how sellers’ credit ratings influence both operational decisions and financing preferences in the supply chain. To this end, we develop a game-theoretic model featuring a capital-limited seller, an e-commerce platform, and a credit-risk-sensitive bank in the presence of both demand uncertainty and credit risk. Our analysis shows that under platform financing, a lower credit rating can lead the seller to increase order quantity. Furthermore, we find that when the unit sourcing cost is high and the commission rate is medium, the platform prefers to offer financing service when the credit rating is either sufficiently high or adequately low. On the other hand, given a low unit sourcing cost and a high commission rate, the seller chooses platform financing when the credit rating is low enough. Finally, we identify two win-win situations where both the seller and the platform favor the same financing scheme.

detail.abstract: Organizational performance is increasingly dependent on technological innovation, especially when it comes to digital governance and public service delivery. The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) in Nigeria was the subject of this study's analysis of technology-led organizational performance. The study, which was based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), used a qualitative thematic approach and gathered data from policy documents, institutional reports, and other pertinent secondary sources. The results show that NIMC's technical initiatives, particularly the National Identification Number (NIN) enrollment system and the integration of identification databases, have strengthened strategy alignment, improved operational efficiency, and improved inter-agency communication. Notwithstanding these advancements, enduring issues like poor ICT infrastructure, a lack of technical capability, financial limitations, and cybersecurity worries still limit performance results. The institution's structural and environmental factors influencing innovation effectiveness were further uncovered by an integrated SWOT-PESTLE analysis. The study comes to the conclusion that although technology innovation significantly improves public sector performance, institutional capacity, enabling regulatory frameworks, and intentional strategy alignment are necessary for its long-term sustainability. By offering policy-relevant insights on how technology innovation might be exploited to improve organizational performance in emerging economies, the article adds to ongoing discussions on public sector digital transformation.

title: Emotion-Adaptive Human-Robot Interaction using Multisensory Cross-Attention Fusion with Multi-Temporal Resolution Convolutional Neural Network

detail.title: Emotion-Adaptive Human-Robot Interaction using Multisensory Cross-Attention Fusion with Multi-Temporal Resolution Convolutional Neural Network
detail.abstract: Recently, emotion-adaptive human-robot interaction (HRI) has been shown to improve the ability of social robots to respond to human emotions accurately. However, existing touch-audio-based recognition models such as multitemporal resolution convolutional neural networks (MTRCNN) have struggled to reliably detect emotional valence owing to the limited discriminative power of tactile sound cues alone. Hence, this study proposes a Multisensory Cross-Attention Fusion with MTRCNN (MCAF-MTRCNN) framework that integrates multimodal sensing to improve valence recognition in emotionadaptive HRI. Initially, synchronized data from the touchproduced audio, facial videos, and speech were collected. These data are preprocessed with Mel-Spectrum Conversion (MSC), Face Detection and Alignment (FDA), z-score normalization to transform raw touch into a time-frequency representation, align the face in each video frame to a standardized position, and standardize feature values across samples. Then, unimodal encoding was performed using MTRCNN, MobileNetV3 with temporal attention, and lightweight wav2vec to independently extract compact feature embeddings for each modality. Furthermore, these embeddings are adaptively fused through bidirectional multihead cross-attention with modality gating to form a robust emotion representation. Finally, multi-class classification predicts gestures, arousal, and valence using an upweighted focal loss for improved valence detection. The proposed MCAF-MTRCNN achieved better results in terms of accuracy (89.42%) than the existing MTRCNN model.

detail.title: Crowded Career Ladders? Intra-Firm Spillovers of Raised Retirement Age

declarations.funderStatement: This study was supported by Charles University, GAUK project No. 333221.

publicationDetails.detailsText: CERGE-EI Working Paper Series No. 810

detail.abstract: I study how delayed retirements reshape firms' internal labor markets, leveraging a German reform that raised women's early retirement age by at least three years. The reform increased retention of older women and reduced both internal promotions and external hiring of younger coworkers, with the greatest losses among middle-aged workers who were near to older workers on the career ladder. Spillovers are structured: promotion crowd-outs arise in thick internal labor markets with intense competition, while hiring declines are largest in thin external markets with high turnover costs. Crowd-out effects concentrate within jobcells, whereas coworkers in different jobcells can benefit when retained older workers possess specific human capital. Taken together, the evidence supports slot-constraint theories-augmented by firm-specific human-capital mechanisms.

title: Virtual Reality as a Promising Opportunity for Tourism in Lebanon: Conceptual Model Diagram Proposed
affiliations: Lebanese University and

detail.title: Virtual Reality as a Promising Opportunity for Tourism in Lebanon: Conceptual Model Diagram Proposed
detail.abstract: Virtual reality emergence in tourism has become a game-changing technological advancement through introducing a new type of immersion and interactive content. In Lebanon, there is scarcity in the research in this area of interest especially with the development of a number of projects that integrated virtual reality, augmented reality and gamification such as Baalbeck Reborn: Temples the only project being officially launched, iHeritage and Med Gaims that are still under progress. This study provides a thorough exploratory, explanatory and descriptive analysis related to the application of virtual reality in one of Lebanon's greatest cultural heritage sites, which helps understand its impact on the cognitive and affective engagement and behavioral intentions. A mixedmethod approach was applied to address the main objective of this study; the qualitative phase was conducted through six semi-structured interviews with key stakeholders, while the quantitative phase involved a questionnaire made over a sample size of 390 participants using the simple random technique. PLS-SEM was employed to understand the influencing variables and the cognitive and affective responses on behavioral intentions. The results showed significant impact of perceived ease of use on affective responses that were additionally one of the strongest mediators with respect to behavioral intentions; perceived usefulness had a well-observed effect on cognitive responses, while authenticity had a great stimulating effect on emotional involvement and flow, which in turn significantly influenced the behavioral intentions. These findings have greatly contributed to the existing literature by integrating essential models including Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) and constructs in the context of virtual reality application. Empirically, the study suggested effective strategies that guide the utility of this technology and highlighted the factors that most shaped tourists' behaviors that all together act as a solid foundation that stakeholders inclusively can rely on for the optimal benefit and ensuring greatest value for tourists' experience. Recommendations for further research in other areas of application of virtual reality and other types of tourism as well.

title: Improving Music Metadata: Towards a Central Repository of Creative Industry, Online Platform and AI Data Resources
affiliations: Institute for Information Law (IViR), University of Amsterdam

detail.title: Improving Music Metadata: Towards a Central Repository of Creative Industry, Online Platform and AI Data Resources
detail.abstract:
With the work notification mechanism in Article 17(4)(b) of the 2019 Directive on Copyright in the Digital Single Market (CDSMD) and the opt-out possibility under Article 4(3) CDSMD, EU copyright legislation seeks to strengthen the position of artists and music companies vis-à-vis online platforms for user-generated content (UGC) and AI developers. From the perspective of copyright data governance, however, these provisions may have unintended side effects. Instead of strengthening the position of artists and music companies, they set in motion metadata streams from the music industry to UGC platforms and AI developers. Ultimately, these metadata streams fortify the data hegemony of large technology companies. They may even increase the dependence of artists and music companies on big tech platforms and AI systems for the distribution of content.

To counterbalance the data hegemony of platforms and AI providers, it is advisable to establish a comprehensive EU music metadata infrastructure – a central data repository that would bundle Article 17(4)(b) work notifications and Article 4(3) opt-out statements that are accompanied by metadata. If these work notifications and opt-out declarations are collected and pooled in a central EU music metadata repository, the resulting accumulation of music data could lead to a promising data reservoir that can compete with the data collections held by platform providers and AI trainers. The music metadata collected at a central EU repository should be enriched with descriptive information on the genre, style and content of the music concerned. They should be made available as an open access data resource to ensure general data accessibility and data transparency for all interested data users. In this way, the establishment of a central EU music metadata repository can support start-ups and ensure equal chances in the metadata arena – regardless of whether an online platform or AI trainer is a small, medium-sized or big company.

title: Cognitive Divergence Theory of AI Adoption

detail.title: Cognitive Divergence Theory of AI Adoption

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Cognitive Divergence Theory of AI Adoption, arguing that for complex tasks, productivity gains from Artificial Intelligence are not evenly distributed but are proportional - often exponentially - to the user's cognitive capacity. Challenging the prevailing "equalizer effect" narrative (which holds true only for short-term, simple tasks), the study integrates empirical behavioral data with a Monte Carlo simulation of 10,000 agents. The findings demonstrate that within 24 months of adoption, the labor market undergoes not gradual stratification, but categorical divergence. The model predicts a productivity collapse for the bottom 50% of the cognitive distribution (due to error rates and rework costs) alongside a threefold output surge for the top 25%, resulting in a massive 71-fold productivity gap. The paper forecasts the emergence of three distinct economic classes by 2028: Homo Symbioticus (the cognitive elite in symbiosis with AI), the Precarious Middle, and the Displaced. Special attention is paid to the specific risks for Eastern European economies, where AI acts as a "Brain Drain Amplifier." Finally, the paper proposes a technical intervention framework: the Mechanism of Cognitive Stimulation (MCS 2.0) to mitigate cognitive atrophy.

title: TRAVEL 3.0: Haggletion Mechanism and Agent-Based Pricing as a New Paradigm in Hospitality Revenue Management

detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper investigates the inefficiencies of traditional hospitality pricing models ("Pricing Blindness") and proposes a novel mechanism, "Haggletion," which integrates seller-controlled haggling with semantic consumer requests. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study analyzes a longitudinal dataset of 4,885 private haggle offers collected between 2020–2025 via the HotelForex platform. We employ a quantitative analysis of acceptance rates, discount elasticity, and lead-time correlations to validate the existence of "Invisible Supply." Findings: Results indicate a 30.3% haggle success rate, confirming high elasticity in hotelier willingness-to-accept (WTA). However, a disconnect is observed between haggle success and final sales conversion (1.1%), attributed to manual operational friction. Behavioral analysis reveals a "Supplier Pain Threshold" at 30% discounts and a counter-intuitive "Aggressive Luxury Paradox" where high-end consumers demand deeper discounts. Originality/Value: The paper introduces the concept of "Travel 3.0," proposing an Agent-Based Architecture where accumulated haggle data serves as a "Ground Truth" oracle for training Large Language Models (LLMs) in autonomous commerce. The findings offer practical implications for hotel revenue managers seeking real-time demand capture strategies in an era of automated commerce.

title: The Geopolitics of Cognitive Divergence - The Resilience Paradox

detail.abstract: Recent industry reports (McKinsey, November 2025) celebrate an unprecedented acceleration in the adoption of Artificial Intelligence, pointing to productivity gains that promise to revitalize the global economy. However, this strictly macroeconomic analysis ignores a hidden, second-order cost: the accelerated erosion of social cohesion. This article, the final installment of the Divergence Theory trilogy, extends the analytical framework from individual psychology to geopolitical stability. We argue that the architecture of Western societies faces a historical paradox. The United States, although the undisputed leader in innovation and efficiency (optimized for the cognitive elite - Tier 1), possesses the most fragile social contract, risking a violent internal fracture as the cognitive middle class becomes economically irrelevant. In contrast, the European Union, often criticized for bureaucratic stagnation and excessive regulation, has institutional mechanisms that act as "shock absorbers", providing a path to social survival, even at the cost of losing technological primacy. The analysis integrates critical variables such as energy constraints, the phenomenon of "cognitive extraction" (a virulent form of brain drain) and the drain) affecting Romania/Eastern Europe and the distinct trajectories of the Asian bloc, providing a map of national security risks for the 2026-2030 horizon.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we develop a new framework in microeconomic theory that explains why consumers frequently choose a lower-utility good over a higher-utility alternative when differences in availability, time delay, and immediate necessity alter the effective value of consumption. While classical utility theory predicts that a consumer who derives greater satisfaction from good A will always prefer A to good B, real-world decisions contradict this assumption repeatedly. We argue that the intrinsic utility of a good is only one component of consumer preference; the time required to obtain a good, the psychological and economic cost of waiting, and the urgency of functional needs collectively reshape the actual utility that guides choice. Building on these insights, we propose two related concepts, Availability-Adjusted Utility (AAU) and Hierarchical Need Utility (HNU), which together form a unified model that explains preference reversals when high-utility goods are heavily delayed while lower-utility goods satisfy immediate needs. Our theory integrates ideas from intertemporal choice, behavioral economics, search theory, and welfare economics, but synthesizes them in a way that has not previously been formalized. Through this work, we aim to offer a more realistic and human-centered account of consumer behavior.

title: Rainfall Shocks and Consumption Risk in Rural India: The Role of Irrigation, Credit, and Employment
affiliations: and Indian Institute of Management Kashipur

detail.title: Rainfall Shocks and Consumption Risk in Rural India: The Role of Irrigation, Credit, and Employment
detail.abstract: Agriculture remains the mainstay of rural livelihoods in India, leaving households highly exposed to rainfall variability. While most studies focus on droughts, often treating excess rainfall as beneficial, both deficits and excesses, as well as delays in monsoon onset and the timing of June-July rainfall, can disrupt household welfare in distinct ways. Using nationwide district-level panel data from 2014 to 2023, this study examines how multiple dimensions of rainfall shocks affect household consumption, not only in aggregate but also across nine categories including food, health, education, and discretionary spending. Methodologically, we combine fixed-effects and quantile regressions with a difference-indifferences strategy that exploits intra-seasonal consumption shifts to identify the buffering role of irrigation, credit access, and non-farm employment. The results show that droughts and delayed monsoons significantly depress consumption, with agricultural households and poorer quartiles most affected, while districts with better groundwater irrigation, credit availability, and non-farm employment opportunities recover more rapidly. These findings highlight the importance of structural conditions in shaping climate resilience and point to policy priorities in irrigation expansion, timely credit provision, and rural non-farm job creation.

title: Psychoeconomic Resilience as the Strategic Foundation of Macrosystems. Human Capital as the Primary Resource of Long-Term Development

detail.abstract:
Psychoeconomic resilience is emerging as a key parameter of macrosystem development amid accelerating global transformations. Based on data collected within the Psychoeconomic Resilience Model (PRM) and the Systemic Influence & Resilience Index (SIRX) between 2020 and 2025, it has been identified that the fundamental variable of long-term economic growth is neither resource availability, nor technological infrastructure, nor institutional configuration, but the distribution of psychological capital within a population. Empirical observations demonstrate that a system’s capacity for innovation, self-renewal, and strategic resilience depends on the prevalence of individuals with an internal locus of control, mature self-regulation, emotional autonomy, and sustained agency under conditions of uncertainty. A deficit of these parameters produces an economy of waiting—characterized by dependence on external stimuli, elevated transaction costs, and reduced adaptive potential.

Field data from PRM reveal that the origin of these differences lies in the quality of the early environment and its ability to support a child’s agency and initiative. Misaligned educational and caregiving practices—such as interpreting initiative as “misbehavior,” forming boundaries through punishment, and failing to recognize giftedness—trigger mechanisms of learned helplessness and shift the locus of control outward. The subsequent decline in self-regulation, cognitive flexibility, memory, attention, and initiative becomes a macroeconomically significant factor, generating intergenerational vulnerability.

A documented case (PRM, 2025) demonstrates that even short-term exposure to an environment lacking competencies in behavioral science and neuropsychology leads to loss of agency, regression of cognitive functions, and a shift toward external control. Restoration of potential becomes possible only after prolonged exposure to a developmentally competent, trust-based, and neuropsychologically informed environment.

The analysis confirms that psychoeconomic architecture is a primary condition of sustainable development rather than its derivative outcome. The PRM framework and the SIRX™ index offer tools for macro-level diagnostics and systemic transformation by cultivating emotional autonomy, agency, initiation, and internal regulation—thus forming human capital capable of generating innovation and sustaining long-term resilience under conditions of strategic uncertainty.

detail.abstract: The paper examines the legal and economic criteria for defining the geographic boundaries of the port cargo handling market under Russian and EU competition law. It reconstructs the approaches of the Federal Antimonopoly Service of the Russian Federation and the European Commission to market definition in port-related cases, with particular attention to the use of demand-side and supply-side substitutability, transport cost differentials and infrastructural constraints. The analysis shows that Russian enforcement practice tends to confine the relevant geographic market to the boundaries of a single seaport or even a single terminal, while often underestimating inter-port competition and the role of hinterland transport alternatives. By contrast, EU practice relies more systematically on the hypothetical monopolist test and on a multi-factor assessment of competitive pressure between ports. The paper identifies the main inconsistencies and gaps in the Russian approach, including the fragmented treatment of private and state-regulated tariffs and the insufficient consideration of contractual switching possibilities for shippers. On this basis, it proposes a structured framework for defining the geographic market in port cargo handling that integrates legal criteria with economic indicators and can be applied in antitrust investigations, merger control and regulatory decision-making. The proposed framework is intended to enhance the predictability and transparency of competition law enforcement in the Russian port sector and to align it more closely with international best practices.

title: Institutional Roots of Poverty in Post-Soviet Economies: A Political Economy Analysis
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Institutional Roots of Poverty in Post-Soviet Economies: A Political Economy Analysis
detail.abstract: Persistent poverty in many post-Soviet states resists conventional policy remedies: despite numerous reform packages, large segments of the population remain economically vulnerable. This paper argues that persistent household vulnerability in transition economies is primarily an institutional phenomenon. Drawing on political-economy theory and six months of mixed qualitative fieldwork in Kyrgyzstan — including 180 days of observation, 150+ interviews and case studies of 12 small manufacturing workshops — I show how institutional legacies, weak contract enforcement, and incentive structures at multiple levels reproduce poverty even when aggregate indicators appear stable. Three mechanisms are central: (1) fragmented and inconsistent regulatory frameworks that incentivise informality; (2) political-economic constraints on implementation that decouple policy design from outcomes; and (3) gendered labour market segmentation that channels educated women and low-skilled workers into unstable employment. The paper situates these findings within the literature on institutions and development (Acemoglu & Robinson; North; Rodrik) and draws implications for policy: reforms must address incentive structures and enforcement capacity, not only formal legislation. The paper concludes with recommendations for institutionally-aware policy design and an agenda for further empirical testing.

title: Religious Identity, Contracts, and Hold-Up Problems
affiliations: University of Vigo - Faculty of Economics and Business

detail.title: Religious Identity, Contracts, and Hold-Up Problems
detail.abstract: This paper explores how principals' identities shape the use of contractual safeguards and the incidence of holdup problems. Using 50,083 apprenticeship contracts registered in Early Modern Venice (1575-1775), I show that masters with a stronger religious identity are significantly less likely to include third-party guarantor clauses. Religious identity is measured using a continuous, name-based index, and the identification strategy exploits exogenous variation in religiosity induced by earthquake exposure before the masters were born. Evidence from apparitions of the Virgin Mary, a regression discontinuity around Pentecost, and heterogeneity analyses points to three complementary mechanisms: beliefs in supernatural monitoring, religious (prosocial) norms, and in-group dynamics. Contrary to the standard prediction that weaker contractual safeguards should increase agent opportunism, religious masters tend to experience fewer holdup problems in the form of apprentice early exit. This result appears to be driven by religious masters hiring more religious apprentices, less opportunistic apprentices self-selecting into contracts with religious masters, and a shift toward relational contracting.

title: Oligopoly in Indian Mineral Exploration: Allocation Design, Entry Barriers, and Policy Consequences
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Shillong

detail.title: Oligopoly in Indian Mineral Exploration: Allocation Design, Entry Barriers, and Policy Consequences
detail.abstract: India's mineral exploration sector exhibits persistent concentration of participation and outcomes, with a small number of public sector undertakings and large private firms dominating access to mineral concessions. This paper argues that such oligopolistic structures are not a natural consequence of geological scale or capital intensity, but are largely policy-induced, arising from the institutional design of mineral rights allocation. Drawing on insights from industrial organization theory and resource economics, the study examines how auction-led allocation mechanisms, stringent eligibility norms, non-transferable exploration rights, and front-loaded financial obligations collectively raise entry barriers and systematically exclude junior exploration firms and risk capital. The resulting market structure constrains competitive discovery, discourages innovation, and weakens the mineral discovery pipeline, particularly for greenfield and critical minerals. The paper further analyzes the economic and governance consequences of concentration, including reduced exploration intensity, strategic hoarding of concessions, inequitable access to sub-surface resources, and long-term resource security risks. Comparative evidence from Canada, Australia, and the United States is used to demonstrate how alternative allocation models-characterized by secure exploration tenure, transferability, and marketled discovery-support broader participation and lower concentration without compromising public interest. The paper concludes by outlining policy reforms aimed at reducing institutional entry barriers, enabling junior explorers, and reorienting India's mineral exploration framework from revenuemaximization towards discovery-led, competitive, and equitable resource governance.

title: Application of the Bolar Exception: Different Approaches in the EU
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Application of the Bolar Exception: Different Approaches in the EU
detail.abstract: This Research Paper addresses the growing problem of access to essential medicines, focusing on the role of intellectual property rights, particularly patent rights, in restricting access by enabling pharmaceutical market monopolies that keep drug prices high. The paper explores the Bolar exception, a legal mechanism designed to allow generic drug manufacturers to seek regulatory approval before a patent expires, thus preventing the de facto extension of patent monopolies. The study examines the transformation of the Bolar exception from a specific legal case into a significant tool of intellectual property, commercial, and pharmaceutical law. The paper analyzes key international legal frameworks and European directives related to the Bolar exception and highlights divergent interpretations of the Exception in German and Polish case law. Through this comparative analysis, the paper argues for the broader implementation of Bolar exceptions to improve access to affordable medicines and reduce healthcare costs.

title: A Value and Character Educational Model: Repercussions for Students, Teachers, and Families
affiliations: Universidad Nacional de Educación a Distancia, España

detail.title: A Value and Character Educational Model: Repercussions for Students, Teachers, and Families
detail.abstract: The aim of this article is to provide some insight on the implementation of a series of values in the educational system. The approach sought is holistic, considering that we weigh the effects of those values not only related to students and teachers, but also to families, government, and school administrators. This approach is new since many values and character education studies are centered on either students or teachers, or both. Also, this article tackles the concept of values and character education, adding the review of several related studies, providing valuable information about the benefits and advantages that this educational model offers based on the expectation that those values must be present in all factors of the learning process. Finally, this article delivers a reflection on those same elements with the goal to use it as a thought-provoking tool to consider more solutions to help students face academic challenges and those related to life.

title: The Ghost in the Math: Why Reswitching Technique is an Economic Impossibility

detail.title: The Ghost in the Math: Why Reswitching Technique is an Economic Impossibility
detail.abstract: The reswitching paradox, a cornerstone of the Cambridge Critique, has long been seen as a fatal flaw in Austrian capital theory. This paper argues that this conclusion is mistaken. We demonstrate that reswitching is a mathematical artifact arising from economically implausible, violently oscillating cost profiles in Sraffian models, not a feature of real capital markets. By introducing a linear capital-structure model that incorporates the entrepreneur's subjective time horizon, we prove the critical payback period is a strictly decreasing function of the interest rate. This monotonic relationship logically precludes reswitching: as interest rates rise, technique preference can shift at most once from capital-intensive to labor-intensive, and never back. The reswitching paradox is thus a phantom menace, affirming the Austrian insight that higher interest rates unambiguously shorten the optimal structure of production.

title: Prophetic Leadership in Academic Institutions: A Catalyst for Positive Transformation and Ethical Excellence

detail.title: Prophetic Leadership in Academic Institutions: A Catalyst for Positive Transformation and Ethical Excellence
detail.abstract: The research focuses on the idea of prophetic leadership in academic institutions. Prophetic leadership shows an unrelenting dedication to promoting a culture of learning, motivating positive change, and upholding social responsibility. Prophetic leadership is typified by transformative leadership practices that encourage good change and a culture of learning and growth. These practices are visionary, moral, and transformative. Due to the fast-shifting global environment, academic institutions have recently faced several challenges. In the face of these challenges, prophetic leadership has emerged as a compelling leadership paradigm that goes beyond conventional approaches. Academic prophets are characterised by their morality, enlightened perspective, and unwavering commitment to fostering positive change both inside and outside of the institution. In this theoretical study, the key characteristics of prophetic leadership are investigated together with the impact on academic institutions, implications on educational outcomes, and social involvement. This paper aims to shed light on the function of prophetic leadership in shaping the future of higher education through a critical analysis of pertinent literature and theoretical analysis.

detail.abstract: This article develops the Taqrib Diagnostic–Decision Model (TDDM) as a formal, multi-dimensional framework for governing Islamic intra-faith rapprochement (taqrib) in a systematic, KPI-governed manner. Building on historical initiatives such as Dār al-Taqrīb and the Amman Message, and on contemporary institutions including the World Forum for Proximity of Islamic Schools of Thought, the study responds to three deficits in current practice: conceptual fragmentation, predominantly narrative documentation, and the absence of explicit measurement and decision-support architectures. Adopting a qualitative, design-science research approach, the article synthesises literatures on conflict transformation, social cohesion, governance of religious diversity, social epistemology and digital religion, together with KPI-based frameworks in Islamic governance. The resulting TDDM is specified as a multi-layer diagnostic–decision system that encodes problem type, level, locus, layer, family, modality and time horizon, and organises them into a coherent architecture for problem classification, portfolio design and performance monitoring. Three illustrative cases local sectarian tension, discriminatory personal-status law and digital hate campaigns demonstrate how TDDM generates tailored, cross-layer intervention bundles with associated indicator families and key performance indicators. The model’s practical implications include audit and planning tools for ministries, taqrib councils and NGOs; structured design of social and legal interventions; and a taxonomy for platform governance and AI-assisted moderation. Theoretically, TDDM reframes taqrib as a system-of-systems design problem and opens a research agenda for data-informed, KPI-driven governance of intra-Islamic diversity.

detail.title: Harmonic Time Theory 2.0: A Unified Ratio-Based Framework for Temporal Expansion, Asymptotic Origins, and Corrected Harmonic Index Domains
detail.abstract: This paper presents the unified and corrected formulation of Harmonic Time Theory, the proposal that physical time is generated by the universe not as a linear quantity but as a harmonic, ratio-based progression analogous to the scaling structure of musical intervals. In this framework, time expands multiplicatively—like octave spacing in frequency—while clocks and calendars impose additive, linear units that do not reflect the true temporal geometry of the universe. This edition consolidates all previous formulations (Parsons 2025a, 2025b), resolves the earlier ambiguity surrounding negative harmonic indices, and introduces a crucial correction: while harmonic indices may extend bidirectionally, physical temporal intervals remain strictly positive and asymptotically approach zero without ever reaching or crossing it. Negative indices describe harmonic positions within the ratio lattice, not physical negative time. Harmonic Time Theory provides a unified explanation for longstanding anomalies in physics, cosmology, and geophysics, including leap seconds, rotational drift, solstice migration, geological acceleration, evolutionary compression, inconsistent cosmic expansion rates, and the illusion of a singular temporal origin. In this framework, the “Big Bang” emerges not as a physical boundary but as a measurement artifact created by applying linear time coordinates to an underlying logarithmic domain. The model is rigorously compared to, and distinguished from, prior research including W.K. George's logarithmic time hypothesis, Barbour’s emergent-time formulations, Nottale’s scale relativity, the Fractal Time Framework, and logarithmic structures in quantum gravity. Harmonic Time Theory provides testable predictions, including exponential trends in timekeeping corrections, harmonic restructuring of cosmological redshift, smoothing of geological and evolutionary timelines under harmonic coordinates, and the resolution of Hubble tension as a measurement mismatch rather than a cosmological anomaly. The resulting formulation offers a coherent, mathematically consistent, and empirically testable foundation for understanding temporal structure, establishing Harmonic Time Theory as a candidate for a new temporal paradigm in physics, cosmology, and scientific measurement.

detail.abstract: This paper presents Epistemic Rigidity, a theoretical framework that integrates multiple cognitive biases to explain individuals’ difficulties in discarding inaccurate information and advancing their knowledge. The framework incorporates the Einstellung effect, Einstein effect, Dunning-Kruger effect, anchoring bias, and additional cognitive and social factors such as confirmation bias, motivated reasoning, cognitive dissonance, heuristics, and the impact of information overload. By examining these interrelated phenomena, Epistemic Rigidity offers a comprehensive understanding of the cognitive barriers to knowledge advancement. This framework applies across various educational, professional, and organizational contexts, providing valuable insights into fostering environments that promote continuous learning, critical thinking, and adopting new ideas. The paper also outlines practical strategies for mitigating these biases, emphasizing the importance of intellectual humility, reflective practice, and diverse information sources.

detail.title: Labor Productivity of Construction Workers in High-Altitude Regions: Influencing Mechanisms and Enhancement Strategies from Workers' Perspectives
detail.abstract: Construction workers in high-altitude regions experience systematic declines in labor productivity due to the combined effects of hypobaric hypoxia and physical workload, with underlying mechanisms that differ markedly from those in plain regions. This study investigates productivity performance and its influence mechanisms among different worker subgroups from the workers' perspective, using regression analysis and path modeling based on field data collected from 154 construction workers on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Results show that the average labor productivity among construction workers is only 26%, with altitude of origin, work experience, age, BMI, and fatigue level identified as key determinants. Path analysis reveals that altitude of origin and work experience positively influence productivity through chain mediation pathways, whereas smoking, alcohol consumption, and age exert negative effects through similar pathways. Fatigue level emerges as the primary constraint on productivity. Furthermore, interactions among smoking, alcohol consumption, BMI, and work experience moderate the strength of these path effects. Simulation modeling identifies the optimal personnel profile: workers originating from altitudes above 3,500 m, aged 25–35, with either <5 or >10 years of work experience, and abstaining from smoking and alcohol-projected to achieve 55% productivity. Sensitivity analysis further confirms altitude of origin and alcohol consumption as key modulating variables. Based on these findings, this study proposes productivity enhancement strategies across three dimensions: personnel allocation, health management, and environmental adaptation. These insights offer both theoretical contributions and practical guidance for construction organization and management in high-altitude regions.

title: Postcolonial Gaslighting and the Framing of Discourse: The Agency of African Nations in the China–Africa Dialogue

detail.title: Postcolonial Gaslighting and the Framing of Discourse: The Agency of African Nations in the China–Africa Dialogue
detail.abstract: Academic and policy debates on Sino–African relations have often marginalized African agency by centering great-power rivalry and portraying China as a neo-colonial threat. This article critically examines how postcolonial gaslighting in Western discourse distorts Sino–African relations, using a critical discourse analysis of media commentary, policy statements, and scholarly narratives. Drawing on discourse studies and postcolonial theory, it integrates the concepts of postcolonial gaslighting and post-truth to reveal how dominant narratives frame Africa as a passive battleground while obscuring historical Western exploitation. The analysis shows that Western commentators frequently employ charged tropes (e.g. “debt-trap diplomacy,” “new colonialism”) that undermine African voices and strategic agency. Examples from a corpus of English-language media and political discourse illustrate this pattern. In contrast, African perspectives and on-the-ground evidence highlight deliberate agency by African states and the tangible benefits of Chinese partnerships in infrastructure and development. The study finds that reductive, Eurocentric framings not only perpetuate outdated colonial stereotypes but also sustain global power asymmetries. It calls for re-centering African viewpoints and a more nuanced, multiperspectival dialogue on China–Africa relations that acknowledges African nations as active protagonists rather than pawns. This has broad implications for international discourse on development and South–South cooperation.

detail.abstract: The Adversity Nexus is a theoretical model elucidating the intricate stages governing the rise and fall of individuals, organizations, and nation-states. This comprehensive framework delves into the paradoxical interplay between progress and stagnation, emphasizing the profound impact of adversity, leadership, growth, abundance, and the pitfalls of overemphasis on security. The model outlines a cyclical progression through key stages: adversity spurs desire for change, leading to the emergence of transformational leaders. These leaders drive growth, resulting in abundance, which in turn creates a focus on safety. However, excessive emphasis on safety breeds stagnation, eventually leading back to adversity. This cycle underscores the delicate balance required to sustain progress and highlights the risks associated with complacency and overprotection. The Adversity Nexus provides valuable insights into the dynamics of success and failure, offering a strategic perspective for navigating the complexities of growth and ensuring resilience against inevitable challenges.

title: Philosophy of Mind & Ontological Engineering

detail.abstract: This treatise challenges the traditional binary distinction between "Dreaming" and "Reality" by shifting the analytical focus from the source of sensory input to the integrated result of the processor. Drawing on the "Black Box" model of human consciousness, I argue that the mind is fundamentally incapable of distinguishing between a "description" of reality and the reality it purports to describe. Through an analysis of autonomous physiological outputs-specifically stress hormones, cardiac responses, and psychosomatic somatization-I propose a new ontological hierarchy: Life is an endless dream, and a dream is a short reality. The paper concludes by framing "Waking Up" not as a transition to objective truth, but as a system-toggle within a singular, persistent cognitive simulation.

Behavior modification has long been a subject of study across psychology, neuroscience,
and leadership development, yet traditional models often fail to account for the emotional
underpinnings that sustain cognitive biases and behavioral patterns. The 3B Behavior Modification
Model addresses this gap by proposing a hierarchical framework in which emotion drives bias, bias
drives belief, belief drives behavior, and behavior drives outcomes. This model challenges conventional
approaches that focus solely on modifying behavior or belief without addressing the foundational role
of bias formation and emotional reinforcement.
This study explores the theoretical foundation of the 3B Model, its conceptual mechanisms, and its
practical applications in leadership, therapy, and decision-making. A qualitative study involving 31
participants from a leadership development program assessed the model's long-term effectiveness.
Findings indicate that 100% of respondents reported continued behavioral progress, with 87% fully
integrating the new mindset and 94% perceiving lasting emotional and cognitive benefits. These results
suggest that interventions targeting emotional biases can lead to more sustainable behavioral changes.
The 3B Model contributes to the field by integrating cognitive science, emotional regulation, and
behavioral psychology into a cohesive framework for change. Its implications extend beyond
leadership development to education, mental health, and organizational transformation. Future research
should further refine and empirically test the model in diverse populations to strengthen its applicability
and theoretical robustness. This article provides a structured analysis of the 3B Model, demonstrating
its value as a comprehensive, scalable, and effective approach to behavior modification.

title: The Future of Smart Contracts in Resolving International Commercial Disputes: A Comparative Analysis within the Framework of International Arbitration

detail.title: The Future of Smart Contracts in Resolving International Commercial Disputes: A Comparative Analysis within the Framework of International Arbitration
detail.abstract: This paper examines the intersection of smart contracts and international commercial arbitration, assessing whether established arbitral frameworks—principally the ICC and ICSID—are equipped to resolve disputes arising from code-based agreements. Drawing on doctrinal analysis, institutional reports, and comparative study of selected jurisdictions (the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, with references to Singapore, Switzerland and China), the research identifies three core challenge clusters: (1) legal recognition and enforceability of purely code-based commitments; (2) interpretive and evidentiary difficulties arising from the technical nature of code and on-chain data; (3) procedural and structural limits within arbitration institutions and within smart-contract design itself. The paper argues that adaptation must be mutual: tribunals and institutions need targeted rule reform, technical literacy, and infrastructure for handling blockchain evidence, while smart-contract design must incorporate flexibility, oracle-risk mitigation and dispute-ready features. Comparative findings show tension between common-law flexibility (which promotes uptake but risks fragmentation) and civil-law formalism (which offers predictability but may slow innovation). The paper concludes with practical reform proposals—hybrid contract models, expert/technical panels, emergency stop mechanisms, and international harmonization efforts—to enable smart contracts to function as reliable instruments of cross-border commerce rather than sources of legal fragmentation.

How to Respond Best?

detail.title:
Managing Demand Leakage in Ride-hailing Platforms:
How to Respond Best?
detail.abstract: Demand leakage occurs in a ride-hailing platform when users cancel and ride off the platform after matching,leading to a loss of revenue for the platform. Using insights from field interviews, we develop an analytical model to capture user decisions regarding off-platform transactions to determine when a ride-hailing platform has the potential for demand leakage in a market. We examine two ways in which a ride-hailing platform can curb demand leakage: reducing price and commissions (only price response - OP) and levying penalties on drivers, while modifying pricing decisions (penalty and price response - PP). While the extant literature suggests that ride-hailing platforms are resistant to demand leakage, we show that the impact of demand leakage on these platforms is dynamic since the fluctuating balance of drivers and riders in the market affects the extent of leakage. We show that demand leakage is higher when the platform’s pricing and commission are meant to increase ride requests, whereas it is lower when it uses surge pricing and increases drivers to meet higher ride requests. Thus, surge pricing reduces the need to respond to demand leakage, whereas the gain from OP and PP response strategies increase when the buffer of drivers is lower in equilibrium. Comparing the OP and the PP response strategies, we find that the PP response strategy is the most effective strategy to curb demand leakage, and leads to the highest profit for the platform. Our study explains why ride-hailing platforms may experience demand leakage under certain conditions, and why the impact of leakage on ride-hailing platforms is distinct. Our study also providesguidance to platforms on selecting the appropriate strategy for managing demand leakage profitably.

title:

affiliations: , NEOMA Business School, IIM Calcutta and Indian Institute of Management Calcutta

detail.title:
Coordinating Retailer-Platform Strategic Choices in Quick Commerce
Partnerships: Does Retailer Commitment Matter and When?
detail.abstract: Quick Commerce (QC) platforms are gaining prominence, particularly in countries such as China and India. It is crucial for QC platforms to partner with local conventional retailers to achieve quick delivery of products. We employ a game-theoretic model in which a platform offers a conventional retailer two partnership models, namely the marketplace model and the dark store model. The conventional retailer could either be a committed or a passive type, classified based on her commitment to maintaining service standards. The retailer chooses either of these models or continues with her existing store operation by not accepting the platform’s partnership offer. We first analyse how the retailer makes her strategic choice. Our findings show that the dark store model becomes more attractive compared to the marketplace model as the retailer’s commitment to service standards increases. The conventional retailer’s preferred strategic choice may differ from the strategic choice that maximises the total supply chain (TSC) payoff. We show how the QC platform should design incentives that align the retailer’s preferred choice with the TSC maximizing choice (coordination), thereby achieving a win-win outcome for both parties. Subsequently, we determine scenarios in which the coordination requires inducing the retailer types to choose the same strategic choice (retailer commitment does not matter), but reward them based on their commitment, or choose different strategic choices (retailer commitment matters). In each of these scenarios, when the QC platform can identify the retailer’s commitment, we show that transfer payments based on the retailer’s type can coordinate the retailer’s choice. When the QC platform cannot identify the retailer’s commitment and there is asymmetry in information, we show how the platform can design effort-based payment menus to reveal the retailer’s type and coordinate the retailer’s choice.

title: Structural Identity Architecture™: The Upstream Model for Leadership Development in the AI-Amplified Era
affiliations: Deliberate Evolution Institute

detail.title: Structural Identity Architecture™: The Upstream Model for Leadership Development in the AI-Amplified Era
detail.abstract: Leadership has historically been developed through downstream strategies: behavior modification, emotional intelligence, communication models, resilience training, and performance frameworks. While effective to a degree, these methodologies share a critical flaw: they assume the leader’s identity, the psychological and biological core that governs perception, decision-making, emotional regulation, and behavior, is stable and aligned. However, identity is not fixed. Identity is structural, composed, and modifiable. It operates as the upstream source code of leadership capacity. When identity misaligns, no amount of downstream skill development can overcome the resulting friction, burnout, emotional volatility, or collapse. This paper introduces Structural Identity Architecture™, the first standardized framework for assessing, stabilizing, and evolving leadership identity through first principles rather than personality theory or psychological interpretation. The system was originally created out of necessity: the author’s own identity collapse occurred after a major personal victory, revealing the absence of a structured, operational identity system within leadership development. Since then, Structural Identity Architecture™ has been tested in two distinct populations, hightrauma reentry participants and high-functioning professionals, with consistent results including rapid clarity, emotional stabilization, reduced internal friction, improved decision quality, and increased leadership alignment. In the context of accelerating technological integration, particularly AI, this upstream identity framework becomes essential. AI does not amplify intelligence, it amplifies identity. Misaligned leaders will produce misaligned outputs at exponential speed; aligned leaders will experience exponential capability. Identity is no longer a philosophical concept, it is the new foundation of leadership effectiveness in the AI era. This paper outlines the conceptual basis, origin story, necessity, and early evidence supporting Structural Identity Architecture™, positioning it as the next frontier in leadership development.

title: Examining retail store strategies in the era of quick commerce: to partner or not to partner?
affiliations: , NEOMA Business School, Indian Institute of Management Calcutta and IIM Calcutta

detail.title: Examining retail store strategies in the era of quick commerce: to partner or not to partner?
detail.abstract: We investigate the optimal partnership strategy for small retailers in a developing economy, where they have the option to either handle product deliveries through their own setup or partner with a quick commerce (QC) platform. To investigate this phenomenon, we first conduct interviews with small retailers in India. Drawing from their insights, we model the interaction between a small retailer and a QC platform using a dynamic game of incomplete information, where the platform lacks knowledge of the retailer’s type. We analyse how factors such as promised delivery lead times, the platform’s business model, and the platform's individual rationality affect a retailer’s decision to partner, focusing on two distinct business models: pure delivery service and commission-based model. We further validate our findings through empirical investigation. Our main findings are as follows: First, retailers encounter a profitability dilemma while deciding whether to partner with a QC platform. Second, the commission-based model helps a QC platform attract more customers by lowering delivery fees. Third, in markets with a high percentage of tech-savvy retailers, an increase in both the share of hasty customers and the customers' per-unit disutility cost makes tech-savvy retailers less likely to partner with a QC platform compared to traditional retailers.

title: Project Communication Management Strategies for Enhancing Cross-Organisational Collaboration in ICIJ Investigative Reports

detail.title: Project Communication Management Strategies for Enhancing Cross-Organisational Collaboration in ICIJ Investigative Reports
detail.abstract: This study builds a conceptual bridge between the disciplines of Project Management (PM) and large-scale, collaborative investigative journalism. It addresses the challenge of applying traditional PM principles to a non-commercial, high-autonomy environment where conventional control mechanisms are unworkable. The research aims to deconstruct the adaptive communication strategies of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ) to understand how they govern their complex, decentralised projects. Adopting a qualitative, single-case study methodology, the research is grounded in empirical data from in-depth interviews with former ICIJ staff and partner journalists (N=11), triangulated with documentary sources. The findings reveal that ICIJ's governance model replaces a traditional, prescriptive Communication Management Plan with a minimalist framework termed 'Framed Autonomy'. This model establishes a set of high-stakes boundaries (the 'frame'), within which partners are empowered to operate with a high degree of autonomy. This structure necessitates a shift in the leadership role from a directive 'Project Manager' to a facilitative 'Organisational Enabler', who cultivates the collaborative ecosystem rather than controlling its processes. The study concludes that in such high-trust networks, communication is repositioned from a supportive function to the primary instrument of project governance itself.

detail.abstract: The development of green entrepreneurship is crucial for addressing environmental issues and fostering economic growth in emerging nations. This study analyzes how artificial intelligence (AI), fintech adoption (FNTA), environmental governance (EG), digital financial capability (DFC), and environmental sustainability (ES) together impact green entrepreneurship (GE). The data for analysis is obtained from WDI and OECD. The data has been sorted out in Excel and then imported into STATA-18. The study utilizes FMOLS, DOLS, GMM, and quantile regression models to analyze both short-term and long-term dynamics. The empirical results show that AI has a significantly negative effect on green entrepreneurship, indicating that high execution costs, energy use, and digital competency gaps constrain its sustainable potential in resource-limited environments. Conversely, fintech adoption, environmental governance, and digital financial capability indicate a strong positive influence, highlighting that including digital finance, effective governance, and financial literacy enhances a venture's ability to secure green financing and implement eco-innovative ideas. Environmental sustainability indicates a weak negative impact, showing that stringent green environments and regulatory costs may limit small setup sustainable startups, especially in developing nations with weak institutional support. The mediation study validates the crucial role of green innovation in transforming technological and financial resources into sustainable startup results, whilst the moderation analysis emphasizes government effectiveness as a significant enabler that enhances these interactions. The outcomes highlight the crucial role of digital financial literacy, the quality of institutions, and technological inclusion in fostering sustainable ventures, particularly within resource-constrained economies. The research emphasizes that digital transformation alone is inadequate; supportive governance and financially inclusive ecosystems are equally crucial for fostering resilient, ecologically responsible firms. The findings provide actionable insights for researchers, governments, and policymakers seeking to integrate finance, technology, and environmental governance to boost green economic transitions.

title: Unpacking Retail Trading Costs: the Role of Options Trading and Limit Order Usage
affiliations: Chapman University - The George L. Argyros College of Business and Economics, Boston College - Department of Finance and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - Department of Finance

detail.title: Unpacking Retail Trading Costs: the Role of Options Trading and Limit Order Usage
detail.abstract: Prior studies of retail trading costs focus on stock market orders, largely overlooking the role of limit orders and the boom in retail options trading. We show that these underexplored factors are critical for assessing overall retail trading costs. First, nonmarketable limit orders account for 17% of stock volume but more than 34% of option volume in Form 606 reports by retail brokers. Second, using trader-level data on 451,299 option and 607,922 stock retail trades, we estimate effective spreads using actual trade direction to average 1.07% for options, much higher than 0.07% for stock trades. But these realized option costs are 60% lower than the 2.59% conventional effective spreads because retail investors commonly use limit orders to reduce trading costs. These patterns hold across trader styles. Finally, individual trader order choices rather than broker defaults drive execution quality, with trader execution performance persisting over time.

detail.title: Ship Satellite Data Reveal Regionalization of Global Supply Chain Networks: Evolving as Complex Adaptive Systems

detail.abstract: Global supply chains are evolving from a highly integrated, globalized structure to a more regionalized one. This transition offers an optimistic outlook for global citizens, as it localizes disruptions and mitigates their impact. While anecdotal evidence has been reported, comprehensive empirical validation of this trend remains limited. In this study, we investigate the structural evolution of the global supply chain network (GSCN) as a complex adaptive system (CAS): each firm independently makes self-driven decisions regarding trade, considering tariff issues, policy changes, and geopolitical factors, and these decisions aggregate and manifest in macro-level evolutionary patterns. To capture such patterns, we utilize large-scale, fine-grained maritime Automatic Identification System (AIS) data from 2015 to 2024. This satellite-based real-time positioning data tracks the global movements of ships, whose activities account for over 80% of the world’s trade by volume. In our analysis, ports serve as nodes and shipments as edges. The data provide clear empirical evidence of regionalization, including shorter paths, increasing clustering coefficients, and modularization patterns. With ports assuming differentiated functional roles, flows within clusters have intensified compared to flows between clusters. The GSCN is shifting towards a structure that enhances local redundancy, global flexibility, and resilience. These findings suggest that re-globalization, rather than de-globalization, is occurring in the form of regionalization.

title: Investigating the Ineffectiveness of Government Policies and Legislation in Mitigating Human-Elephant Conflict in the North Central Province of Sri Lanka

detail.title: Investigating the Ineffectiveness of Government Policies and Legislation in Mitigating Human-Elephant Conflict in the North Central Province of Sri Lanka
detail.abstract: Human-Elephant Conflict (HEC) has become a critical socio-environmental issue in the North Central Province of Sri Lanka, posing significant threats to both rural communities and elephant populations. Despite the implementation of various government policies and legislative measures, the conflict continues to escalate, leading to loss of human lives, destruction of property, and declining elephant populations. This study investigates the ineffectiveness of existing government policies and legislation in mitigating HEC, focusing on the gaps between policy formulation and practical implementation. A qualitative research approach was adopted, utilizing in-depth interviews with key stakeholders, including government officials, conservationists, and affected community members. The findings reveal five major barriers to effective policy implementation: lack of coordination between government agencies, inadequate community involvement, insufficient funding and resource allocation, ineffective enforcement of wildlife protection laws, and socio economic challenges faced by rural populations. Additionally, the study highlights how conflicting interests between conservation efforts and agricultural expansion exacerbate the situation. The research emphasizes the urgent need for a more integrated and community-driven approach, with improved policy enforcement, sustainable land-use planning, and increased stakeholder engagement to develop long-term solutions for HEC mitigation in Sri Lanka.

detail.abstract: The debate over whether colonialism or neocolonialism is "lesser of evil than the other " in Africa is a complex and multifaceted discourse that examines the enduring impacts of both systems on the continent's development. Colonialism, characterized by direct foreign domination and exploitation, left an indelible mark on African societies, dismantling indigenous structures and imposing artificial borders that fostered ethnic tensions and socio-political instability. In contrast, neocolonialism often perceived as a subtler form of control manifests through economic dependencies, political manipulation, and cultural hegemony, perpetuating inequalities established during the colonial era. This paper critically evaluates the legacies of both colonialism and neocolonialism, exploring how each has contributed to the ongoing subjectivity of African nations within a global context. This research study gathered and analysed qualitative data from a wealth of online literature sources. The study selected 22 peer-reviewed articles spanning from 1900 to 2024, each discussing "Which is the lesser of two evils", Colonialism or Neocolonialism, in Africa? This study revealed the complex and multifaceted discourse that examines the enduring impacts of both systems on the continent's development. The qualitative research methodology applied in this study aimed to provide valuable insights into the struggles and challenges faced by African leaders to eradicate colonialism and neo-colonialism in institutional governance, and the paper aimed to shed light on how external forces shaped African governance. The study reveals that while colonialism inflicted immediate and visible damage, neocolonialism operates insidiously, maintaining control through mechanisms such as foreign aid, multinational corporations, and international financial institutions. The implications of this ongoing power imbalance are profound, stifling local agency and inhibiting sustainable development. This research aims to illuminate the complexities of colonial and neocolonial legacies, ultimately arguing that while neither system can be deemed "better," understanding the nuanced interplay of both is essential for framing effective strategies for African empowerment and self-determination. By confronting these historical and contemporary injustices, African nations may strive towards defining their own paths to sovereignty and sustainable growth.

title: Virtuous or Vain? Complexity in Equity-Premium Forecasting

detail.title: Virtuous or Vain? Complexity in Equity-Premium Forecasting
detail.abstract: The recent debate on the "virtue of complexity" in equity-premium forecasting raises a practical question: when does additional flexibility generate genuine timing skill, rather than simply amplifying noise or embedding passive exposures? Using the Goyal-Welch (GW) macro-financial predictors, we reevaluate linear benchmarks, Random Fourier Feature (RFF) ridge regression, exact Gaussian RBF kernel ridge regression (KRR), and shallow neural networks within a common empirical framework. We quantify performance using both the information coefficient and the Sharpe ratio of a market-timing payoff. First, we show that the RFF expansion-at the heart of the debate-induces a covariance geometry with a large near-null space and a broad active spectrum, consistent with substantial overfitting risk. Second, in the moderate-n GW setting, exact RBF KRR is both more performant and dramatically faster as a nonlinear benchmark, calling into question the need for large RFF discretizations. Third, at similar (and sometimes lower) levels of complexity than RFFs, shallow neural networks deliver superior out-of-sample performance, although many of the top-performing networks are statistically indistinguishable from one another. Finally, using demeaned-weight payoffs and a mean-covariance decomposition, we show that strong models' Sharpe ratios are driven primarily by covariance (timing skill), rather than by passive mean-exposure artifacts that can arise with non-centered targets and/or no-intercept specifications.
